{{nihongo|'''Uchi Shrine'''|内神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in Uchisato Uchi, {{ill|Yawata|Q260923|qid=Q260923}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|Q120730|qid=Q120730}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}, and under the former {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=shrine ranking system}} it was a {{ill|Son-sha|Q134917284|qid=Q134917284}}. {{nihongo|'''Uchi Shrine'''|内神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Yamashiro Province]].

== Enshrined deities ==
; Yamashiro no Uchi no Omi (やましろのうちのおみ)
: Also written "Yamashiro no Uchi no Omi."
; {{ill|Umashiuti-no-Sukune|Q18225727|qid=Q18225727|lt=Umashiuchi-no-Sukune}} (うましうちのすくね)
: Also written as "Amamiuchi-no-Sukune" in documents. He is the half-brother of {{ill|Takenouchi no Sukune|Q1073668|qid=Q1073668}} and ancestor of the Yamashiro Uchi no Omi. He is enshrined in the co-seat.

== History ==
Shrine tradition says the shrine was founded after the death of Yamashiro no Uchi no Omi. Umashiuchi-no-Sukune, enshrined in the co-seat, is thought to have been later merged as ancestral deity of Yamashiro no Uchi no Omi<ref>See Yawata Tourism Association page in external links.</ref>. Details of Yamashiro no Uchi no Omi are unclear; it may be a clan name rather than personal name. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|Q1045362|qid=Q1045362}} there is an entry for a clan "Uchi no Omi" descended from Prince {{ill|Hikofutsuoshi no Makoto no Mikoto|Q11487911|qid=Q11487911}}, son of {{ill|Emperor Kōgen|Q333572|qid=Q333572}}.

In the {{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Engi}} 5 ({{ill|927|ab|927|af|927|am|927 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|927|ar|927|ary|927|ast|927|avk|927|az|927|azb|۹۲۷ (میلادی)|bar|927|bcl|927|be|927|be_x_old|927|bg|927|bn|৯২৭|bpy|মারি ৯২৭|br|927|bs|927.|ca|927|cdo|927 nièng|ceb|927|ckb|٩٢٧|crh|927|cs|927|csb|927|cv|927|cy|927|da|927|de|927|el|927|eml|927|eo|927|es|927|et|927|eu|927|fa|۹۲۷ (میلادی)|fi|927|fo|927|fr|927|fy|927|ga|927|gan|927年|gd|927|gl|927|he|927|hi|927|hr|927.|ht|927 (almanak jilyen)|hu|927|hy|927|id|927|ilo|927|io|927|is|927|it|927|ja|927年|jv|927|ka|927|kaa|927|kk|927 жыл|ko|927년|la|927|lb|927|lij|927|lmo|927|lt|927 m.|lv|927. gads|map_bms|927|mdf|927|mg|927|mhr|927|mi|927|mk|927|mr|इ.स. ९२७|mrj|927 и|ms|927|mzn|۹۲۷|nah|927|nap|927|nds|927|new|सन् ९२७|nl|927|nn|927|no|927|nrm|927|nso|927|oc|927|or|୯୨୭|os|927-æм аз|pl|927|pnb|927|pt|927|qu|927|ro|927|ru|927 год|rue|927|sa|९२७|scn|927|sd|927ع|se|927|sh|927.|shn|927|si|927|sk|927|smn|927|sq|927|sr|927|su|927|sv|927|sw|927|tg|Соли 927|th|พ.ศ. 1470|tk|927|tl|927|tly|927|tr|927|tt|927 ел|uk|927|ur|927ء|uz|927|vec|927|vi|927|war|927|wuu|927年|xmf|927|zh|927年|zh_min_nan|927 nî|zh_yue|927年|qid=Q30470}}) {{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}} {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932}}, it is listed in {{ill|Tsuzuki District, Kyoto|Q1154678|qid=Q1154678}}, {{ill|Yamashiro Province|Q749276|qid=Q749276}}, as "two seats of Uchi Shrine," and is ranked as shikinaisha. In the {{ill|Middle Ages|Q12554|qid=Q12554}}, it was called "Kasuga Munakata Shrine."

According to the {{ill|jinjameisaichou|Q11590704|qid=Q11590704}}, it suffered war damage in the {{ill|Muromachi period|Q334845|qid=Q334845}} during Daiei-era conflicts and was moved to the current location in the Tenshō era. The old site was southeast of the present shrine and remains in the place name "Uchisato Furumiya."

From Oct 2001 to Sep 2002, current honden and precinct were improved as the "Uchisato district construction project."

== Precincts ==
[[File:Uchi-jinja (Yawata) honden.jpg|thumb|200px|right|Honden]]
The precinct is at the west edge of the Uchisato settlement, surrounded by rice fields. The honden is one-bay {{ill|Nagare-zukuri|Q210684|qid=Q210684}} with copper-sheet roof, built in 2002.

An old honden stands to the left of the current honden. Like the present honden, it is one-bay nagare-zukuri with copper roof. During the 2001-2002 works it was relocated and preserved from the current honden site. At that time an ink inscription dated {{ill|Kanpō|Q1145798|qid=Q1145798}} 3 ({{ill|1743|Q7580|qid=Q7580}}) was found, helping identify its construction period. The building is registered as a Kyoto Prefecture cultural property.
